title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: Grothendieck's programme on Dieudonné theory of Barsotti–Tate (p-divisible) groups via crystals, the material of his ICM 1970 talk and Montréal 1970 lectures, carried out in Messing's thesis (LNM 264, 1972). The previous page attached to each BT group G over S (p locally nilpotent) its Dieudonné crystal D*(G). Its value on S carries a Hodge filtration 0 → ω_G → D*(G)_S → t_{G*} → 0. This filtration is functorial in G and compatible with base change.

This page:
(1) It defines a 'filtered F-V-crystal on S': an F-V-crystal in locally free modules M together with a locally direct-summand submodule of M_S. This gives a functor BT(S) → F-V-cris fil(S), compatible with pullback.
(2) Remark: the filtration ω_G ⊂ D*(G)_S is the analogue of the Hodge filtration on relative first de Rham cohomology. A deleted draft was about to explain this via G = A(∞) = lim A(n) for an abelian scheme A/S, i.e. D*(A(∞))_S ≅ H^1_dR(A/S) with Fil^1 = ω_A.
(3) Deformation problem. Let S' ⊃ S be a PD thickening. The crystal property gives D*(G')_{S'} = D*(G)_{S'} = D*(G_o)_{S'}, where S_o is the reduction mod p and S' is viewed in the absolute crystalline site of S_o. So lifts G' of G correspond bijectively to locally direct-summand submodules of D*(G)_{S'} lifting ω_G.
(4) Theorem (Grothendieck–Messing deformation theorem): BT(S') → {pairs (G on S, locally direct summand Fil ⊂ D*(G)_{S'} lifting ω_G)} is an equivalence of categories. A handwritten addition restricts this to S' being a nilpotent PD thickening, or to infinitesimal (connected) G. This is exactly the hypothesis in Messing's published version.
(5) If Problem 1 has a positive answer, one gets a description of BT(S) for p locally nilpotent by filtered Dieudonné crystals. Problem 1 asks whether D* is an equivalence in characteristic p onto admissible F-V-crystals. The step is to apply the deformation theorem to (S_o, S), using that pO_S is a PD ideal. The next page adds that the general (S, S') case reduces formally to (S_o, S) via Crisloclib(S) ≅ Crisloclib(S_o).
errors: Gap/subtlety: the handwritten restriction to nilpotent PD thickenings conflicts with the planned application to the pair (S_o,S) for p = 2. The canonical divided powers on pO_S are not nilpotent when p = 2, since v_2(2^n/n!) = s_2(n) does not grow. So the reduction of BT(S) to filtered crystals over S_o needs extra care at p = 2 (or a restriction to infinitesimal groups). This difficulty is known from Messing and later work of Zink and Lau.

The equality D(G')_{S'} = D*(G)_{S'} tacitly requires the PD structure on the ideal of S in S' to be compatible with the canonical one on p. Grothendieck flags this only by the parenthetical about the absolute crystalline site of S_o.
Minor slip in the typescript: 'une sous-module' should read 'un sous-module'; 'classes d'isomorphie cherchés' should read 'cherchées'.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a draft of the well-known Grothendieck–Messing deformation theorem and the filtered-crystal programme, all published (ICM 1970, Montréal lectures, Messing 1972). The only details of mild interest are the handwritten nilpotency/infinitesimal restriction, which matches Messing's final hypothesis, and the deleted abelian-scheme example; neither is new.
transcription_corrections: The handwritten addition after 'équivalence de catégories' reads approximately: 'si S' est à p. div. nil ou si on se borne à des G' qui sont infinitésimaux'. The 'Remarques' and 'infinitésimaux' fragments belong to the same insertion, which continues further along the line.
In 'D(G')_{S'}' the prime on G is a later handwritten addition.
The left-margin pencil note (beside the BT(S) → F-V-cris fil(S) functor) is barely legible, roughly 'Faut-il [libre?] ... (? on va ... [rassembler?])'; the transcription's reading is uncertain.
The deleted text reads 'partons par exemple d'un schéma abélien A sur S, et prenons G = A(∞) = lim A(n). On peut alors', which is consistent with the given transcription.
